correctness.rationale: Complete type recurrence T_{r+1}=(atomic_signature,set of one-point-extension T_r types) is proved equivalent to r-round Ehrenfeucht--Fraisse equivalence, with repeated vertices. Exhaustive integer C++17 enumeration of all path-square orders 1..47 yields classes min(n,11) at rank 3 and min(n,26) at rank 4. A separate Python implementation reproduces orders 1..12 and the 25/26/27 critical boundary. A gap invariant with B_r=3*2^r proves all orders >=47 rank-four equivalent and >=23 rank-three equivalent. Transitivity bridges to exact infinite thresholds. The finite calculations do not assert infinite results alone.

originality.rationale: Search and primary-source comparison found ordinary-path EF classifications (Brown--Hoshino), qualitative FO model checking on interval/unit-interval graphs (Ganian et al.), quantifier-count rather than quantifier-rank games (Fagin et al.), and Ramsey numbers rather than logical types of squared paths (Allen et al.). Direct searches for P_n squared, path powers, unit interval graphs, quantifier rank 3/4 and thresholds 11/26 found no exact prior theorem. A related published directed-path theorem concerns a distinct language and different cutoff. Novelty is assessed under accessible evidence; not certified globally.

value.rationale: For a fundamental bounded-bandwidth unit-interval family, a complete pair of exact logical spectra is a natural invariant that measures the finite-order information visible at depth three and four. The sharp rank-four bound 26 is strictly below the elementary uniform game upper bound 47, so establishing it requires a nontrivial finite classification in addition to a uniform infinite strategy. It is neither a small arbitrary census nor implied by the earlier classification of ordinary paths or squared cycles; the endpoint effect is substantive. The theorem is explicitly limited to two ranks and the adjacency/equality language.
